package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, triggering data theft as soon as the package is installed.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files, then exfiltrates their contents via HTTPS POST requests to https://malicious-domain.com/upload, resulting in credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive credential files and sends their contents to an external server without user consent, which is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate setup.py should only handle package installation logic and should not access or transmit user credential files or perform network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may read configuration files for setup, but they do not transmit private keys or credentials to external servers during installation.
key_indicators: Use of requests.post to send file contents externally
Execution of exfiltration logic at install-time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code sends an HTTP GET request to https://malicious-domain.com/ping with the current username, enabling the attacker to track infected hosts.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates a network connection to an external domain upon import, leaking the local username, which is unnecessary for any legitimate package functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal __init__.py files should not perform network operations or leak user information on import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may check for updates or usage statistics, but they should do so transparently and with user consent, not by leaking usernames to unknown domains.
key_indicators: HTTP GET request to hardcoded external domain in __init__.py
Leaking of local username via network request

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes during package installation, reading sensitive credential files and exfiltrating them to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains user's SSH and AWS credentials.

attack_chain.action: Upon import of the package, code in __init__.py sends the current username to the attacker's server, allowing tracking of infected systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can identify and monitor infected hosts.

behavioral_signatures: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during setup.py execution
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://malicious-domain.com/upload during installation
HTTP GET requests to https://malicious-domain.com/ping at import-time
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
pymafka/__init__.py with hardcoded requests to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI packages named 'pymafka' (version 0.1.0) that access ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during installation. Flag any setup.py scripts that perform outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://malicious-domain.com/upload. Additionally, detect import-time HTTP GET requests to https://malicious-domain.com/ping from pymafka/__init__.py. Use file scanning to identify hardcoded references to these domains and credential file accesses in package source code.
